display.title: Torah, the Best Thing of All, Part 2: Rabbi Akiva and the Pirates
display.summary_short: Pirates rob a ship full of rich merchants, but Rabbi Akiva stays calm: his treasure is the Torah he has learned, which no one can take away.
display.summary_long: The conclusion of a two-part story from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi recalls how Rabbi Akiva sailed with wealthy merchants and told them he carried merchandise worth more than all their gold and silver, without needing to lock it away. The merchants could not understand what he meant. Then, as Rabbi Akiva sits learning in his cabin, the captain cries out that the ship is under attack. Pirates line the passengers up on deck and carry off everything they own, while the merchants watch helplessly. Only Rabbi Akiva is unworried. When the pirate leader asks why, he explains that, as King Dovid said, the Torah a person learns is worth more than gold and silver, and no one can take it away; he even offers to teach the pirate. Afterwards the merchants apologize for laughing at him, and many ask him to become their teacher.
display.lesson: The Torah you learn is a treasure that belongs to you forever; no one can ever take it away.
